Privacy policy

Observation screen

Intensity profile

Horizontal cut at y = 0; normalized to its own peak.

How this bench works

Light starts as mutually incoherent Gaussian emitters, passes through a soft Gaussian condenser aperture and a thin amplitude mask, then an ideal two-lens 4f relay.

Each emitter’s field is propagated separately; intensities are added. The illumination pupil (source shape) sets the distribution of illumination directions. The separate projection aperture filters spatial frequencies. Near the mask, scalar diffraction is calculated; intermediate relay planes use the Fresnel–Collins integral.

Physical appearance
Lens curvature, mounts and plate thickness are illustrations. The equations use ideal thin lenses, not real glass surfaces.
Scale
The distance ruler is physical. Component heights are enlarged. Only the local mask window is simulated, with zero transmission outside it.
Accuracy
This is a low-NA scalar teaching model. It omits polarization, material effects and lens aberrations. Preview uses fewer pixels and source samples; use Fine and compare results for sampling sensitivity.
Brightness
Local scaling shows shape, not comparable power. Shared scaling uses a fixed reference: the largest source, mask-incident, aperture-plane or image intensity. Log views show −120 to 0 dB. Source weights and openings have their own scale. Yellow indicates illumination; blue indicates projection. These colours do not represent a change in wavelength. Ray count does not represent intensity.
Compared with MATLAB
The browser has five introductory experiments and four independently positioned observation views on desktop. MATLAB additionally offers saved comparison windows, more presets, a plate-scale comparison, finer pattern painting and more automatic numerical checks.
Browser edition
The numerical routines are translated from the MATLAB project and checked with numerical benchmarks. XY, XZ and YZ use the same spatial and source sampling at each detail level. Fine uses a 512 × 512 mask grid, 2× propagation padding and 25 × 25 source bins (445 weighted emitters for the default circular source). The full path samples z adaptively; near-mask diffraction uses 61 planes. For converged results, refine both spatial and source sampling. All five presets include saved Fine key-position images and both full-path wave cuts. The aperture plane is additionally sampled on a dense local grid; display smoothing does not change numerical profile values. Updated calculations run on your device.
